opener: Lord, I didn't expect the attack to come from inside my own camp. I expected the enemy to come after what I had — I didn't expect the people closest to me to come after who I am, and to do it on the one day I had nothing left to defend myself with.
paragraphs: They don't know what it cost me to keep showing up. They only know what's missing now — the plan that didn't work, the thing that burned, the trust that's gone — and instead of helping me carry it, some of them have started looking for someone to blame instead, and I'm the nearest name they can find. I'm tired, Lord, and I'm outnumbered in more ways than one: outnumbered by the loss itself, and outnumbered by the voices deciding this is somehow my fault.

So tonight I'm doing what David did at Ziklag before anyone gave him permission to feel strong again — I'm encouraging myself in You, right here, before the blame talk even finishes its sentence. I don't need every person in my camp to believe in me before I believe You. Let the same God who turned a devastated man into a man who pursued, overtook, and recovered everything meet me in this exact spot: surrounded, blamed, and still Yours. Give me back more than what was taken, and give me back more than anyone around me expects to see return. In Jesus' name, amen.
kicker: A Prayer For When Your Own People Turn On You
footerNote: Save this for the day the blame came from people who were supposed to be on your side
